Definition: The longitudinal pattern of the disorder recorded as the final diagnosis, across the whole documented course from onset to death. An episode is a period in which the disorder was clinically manifest at or above diagnostic threshold. Two episodes are distinct only if separated by at least two consecutive months below threshold, following the DSM criterion for separating recurrent major depressive episodes. Score 1 only if the single episode ended and the donor remained below threshold until death or the end of documentation. A single episode that never remitted is continuous, not single. Score 2 if at least two distinct episodes occurred at any point in the course, including when the illness later became persistent; a change in the level between episodes is captured in Interepisode state. Score 3 if, from onset onwards, there was never a period of at least two months below threshold.
Options: 1: single episode, 2: episodic, 3: continuous, NA: no psychiatric disorder, ND: course cannot be established from the record
Derivation rule: Will be checked against a derived version once the episode definition exists.
Notes: Together, Course pattern and Interepisode state are a transdiagnostic application of the ICD-10 course specifiers for schizophrenia (fifth character of F20) and the DSM-IV-TR longitudinal course specifiers with and without full interepisode recovery.

Definition: The level of symptoms and functioning reached between episodes, or after the episode for a single-episode course, for the disorder recorded as the final diagnosis. For a continuous course, it describes whether the persistent symptoms and impairment remained stable or increased over time. Full remission means no more than minimal symptoms, with functioning back at the premorbid level: work, study, household and relationships resumed as before. Incomplete remission means clinically relevant symptoms or impairment persisted between episodes, without clearly increasing over time. Progressive deficit means the residual symptoms or impairment clearly increased over the course, for example a lower level of functioning after later episodes than after earlier ones, or a loss of work, housing or independence that was not regained. Where the state differed between episodes without a clear increase, score the predominant state. Impairment attributed in the record to a neurodegenerative disease, a brain injury or another somatic illness is not counted as deficit here. Score 0 is not possible for a continuous course.
Options: 0: full remission, 1: incomplete remission with stable residual symptoms or deficit, 2: progressive deficit, NA: no psychiatric disorder, ND: interepisode state cannot be established from the record
Notes: Together, Course pattern and Interepisode state are a transdiagnostic application of the ICD-10 course specifiers for schizophrenia (fifth character of F20) and the DSM-IV-TR longitudinal course specifiers with and without full interepisode recovery.

Definition: Duration of the longest uninterrupted period in which the disorder recorded as the final diagnosis was clinically manifest at or above diagnostic threshold. The same rule as in Course pattern applies: the period is only interrupted by at least two consecutive months below threshold. Improvement that did not last two months, or that left the donor still above threshold, does not interrupt it. A period still ongoing at death counts up to the date of death. Where only an approximate duration can be established, for example “al jaren ernstig depressief”, score the band the record most plausibly supports and quote the passage in the evidence text.
Options: 1: less than 6 months 2: 6 to less than 12 months 3: 12 to less than 24 months 4: 2 to less than 5 years 5: 5 to less than 10 years 6: 10 years or more NA: no psychiatric disorder ND: duration cannot be established from the record
Derivation rule: Longest run of observations without a gap longer than the episode definition.

Definition: Number of episodes during which catatonia or catatonic features were documented. Old variable(s): No. of episodes of catatonia/catatonic features
Derivation rule: Count of distinct catatonia observation periods.

Definition: Number of documented delirium episodes at any point in life.

Definition: Any further indication of severity described in the file that the structured fields do not capture.

Definition: Global severity of illness on the Clinical Global Impression scale, rated at the worst moment.

Definition: Global severity of illness on the Clinical Global Impression scale, rated at moment of death.

Notes: Rescaled from 0-6 to the published CGI-S 1-7.

Definition: Clinical staging of the disorder, following the transdiagnostic staging model.
Options: 0 = No current symptoms; increased risk of disorder; 1a = Mild or non-specific symptoms; 1b = Moderate but sub-threshold symptoms; 2 = Full-threshold disorder with moderate to severe symptoms; 3 = Incomplete remission or relapse; 4 = Severe illness, unremitting, or refractory, ND
Notes: https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lanpsy/article/PIIS2215-0366%2824%2900060-9/fulltext ND added.

Definition: Forensic manner of death, recorded independently of the medical cause.
Options: 0: natural, 1: suicide, 2: euthanasia/physician-assisted suicide, 3: accidental (including unintentional overdose), 4: homicide, 5: undetermined, ND
Notes: Separating manner from medical cause resolves where euthanasia belongs: it is a manner, not a cause. Released alongside illness duration and severity at death, since death is partly independent of the illness.

Definition: Direct medical cause of death as documented.

Definition: Extent to which psychiatric illness contributed to death.

Notes: Independent of manner of death; captures the excess-mortality question.

Definition: Where euthanasia was granted: the primary grounds.
